description: Advances: specled.package — advisory findings from the specled_-6fn test-critic pass, deferred out of that ticket as future hardening of test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs. (A3) The token patterns lead with a (?<![\w/]) negative lookbehind to keep a finding-code-shaped token from matching inside a file path. Its bounds are unbounded and untested: ANY token preceded by / is skipped, so e.g. foo/append_only/deep_fabricated is not flagged. Add boundary tests pinning both directions — the closure-file path segment .../config/branch_guard_test.exs stays suppressed AND a real backtick-delimited code is still caught — so tightening or loosening the lookbehind cannot silently change coverage. (A4) severity_corpus/0 deliberately excludes .spec/** because spec scenarios quote atom-form config as the input under test; real atom-form severities exist at .spec/specs/prose_guard.spec.md, branch_guard.spec.md and spec_drift_trailer.spec.md, so the exclusion is load-bearing but unasserted. Assert the asymmetry: an atom-form severity in a guidance doc trips, the same form under .spec/** does not. Collapsing severity_corpus into finding_code_corpus would start false-positiving with no test warning. (A5) The token char-class [a-z_] cannot represent a finding code containing a digit. Not a current defect (no emitted code has one), but if one is ever added the hand-maintained @known_codes mirror and the extraction pattern silently diverge. Decide whether to widen the class or assert that no emitted code contains a digit.

comments.text: Additional findings from the specled_-6fn ship-it critical review (2026-07-23), same hardening theme: (1) COVERAGE GAP — the lint guards 3 of at least 5 emitted code namespaces; evidence/*, detector_unavailable and spec_requirement_too_short are unguarded (the corpus happens to be clean today). Either widen @token_patterns to cover them or narrow the must to claim only what is guarded. (2) STALE-MARKER CHECK — nothing detects an allow-marker whose token has since become a real emitted code, or whose token no longer appears on its line; such a marker silently rots into a permanent unearned exemption. (3) MIRROR IS FAIL-LOUD ONLY ONE WAY — @known_codes catches a code ADDED to lib/ but not one DELETED from it: docs naming a now-dead code keep passing. (4) PRE-EXISTING SPEC INACCURACY (not introduced by 6fn, deliberately left rather than silently widened) — .spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md scenario given:/when: claim a mix spec.check branch run with mix spec.cover.test fixture coverage that the covering test (test/integration/scenario_test_only_change_test.exs) never performs; it calls CoverageTriangulation.findings/3 on hand-built maps. 6fn reconciled only the then: clause, which was the fabricated-code defect in scope. Note append_only detect_scenario_regression/3 compares scenario COUNTS, so it cannot see then-clause content — a clean spec.check is weak evidence for scenario-text accuracy.

Go-live triage 2026-07-25: the two LIVE spec inaccuracies (package.spec.md overclaiming must; triangulation.spec.md fabricated scenario) split out to P1 gate ticket specled_-cz0. This ticket now holds only the deferred hardening items (A3 lookbehind bounds, A4 severity-corpus asymmetry, A5 digit codes, stale-marker sweep, two-way mirror) — stays P2, post-launch.

Deferred widening identified while fixing specled_-cz0 (2026-07-25), belongs with the rest of the lint hardening here.

cz0 widened the doc-identifier lint from three guarded finding-code families to five, adding evidence/* (7 codes) and cross_field/* (8 codes). Those were the only remaining families carrying a namespace or ratified prefix — verified by extracting every code-shaped literal from lib/ (99 distinct) and grouping by prefix.

Two further clusters COULD be guarded and were deliberately left out of cz0:
  - surface_target_* (3 codes)
  - scenario_cover_* (2 codes)

Both currently collide with zero non-code identifiers in the scanned corpus, so a stem pattern would not false-positive today. That is the entire reason they are candidates — and also the reason to be careful, since "clean today" is exactly the property cz0 existed to stop relying on.

The larger bare-code stems are NOT candidates; measured against the corpus they each reject correct prose:
  detector_    → detector_unavailable_by_leg (review-output field) + a requirement id embedding the stem
  decision_    → 8 non-codes (decision_dir, decision_governance, decision_index, ...)
  verification_→ 4 non-codes
  requirement_ → 6 non-codes

Cost of the widening: two more hand-maintained allowlists. specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus rejects deriving the code set by reflection over lib/, so there is no cheap way to keep them honest — which is why this pairs naturally with the two-way mirror and stale-marker items already scoped here.

Second item for this ticket's two-way-mirror scope, surfaced by cold verification of specled_-cz0 (2026-07-25).

The link between specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity and the ADR that governs its enforcement boundary is one-way:

  - .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md declares `affects: specled.package`
  - .spec/specs/package.spec.md `decisions:` lists declarative_current_truth, local_skill_scaffold, explicit_subject_ownership, guided_reconciliation_loop — but NOT doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus

Consequence, and why it is worth fixing rather than just noting: the must states which finding-code families are mechanically guarded, and the ADR is where the deliberate non-guarding of surface_target_* and scenario_cover_* is disclosed and justified. A reader who stops at the must has no in-corpus pointer to that disclosure. cz0 mitigated this by rewording the must so it cannot be read as claiming exhaustive coverage (commit b7b9eb1), but the mitigation is prose discipline, not a link — the next author to touch either file has nothing mechanical telling them the two are coupled.

This is the same defect shape already scoped here as the two-way mirror (@known_codes catches a code ADDED to lib/ but not one DELETED), one level up: subject → decision references are checked in one direction only, so a spec can silently lose its pointer to the ADR that qualifies it.

title: Harden doc-identifier lint: lookbehind bounds, severity-corpus asymmetry, digit-bearing codes
